name: The Home Counties
description: A single-player extraction shooter in a near-future Britain at war. Raid the Bletchley streets the government emptied and the gangs took over, then reach the red smoke before the timer runs out.
tagline: The government moved on. The gangs moved in. Take what you can carry from Bletchley's empty streets, and reach the red smoke before the clock runs out...

story.heading: How it got this way
story.intro: Nobody bombed Duncombe Street. It was emptied, then taken.

beats.title: Britain kept the war supplied
beats.text: Russia launched a full-scale invasion into Europe, and Britain became NATO's logistics hub. American and allied troops, vehicles, rifles, helmets and body armour came through its ports, airbases and depots by the shipload.

beats.title: Russia paid for trouble
beats.text: Britain was already divided, worn down by COVID, heatwaves, cyberattacks and one political crisis after another. Russia saw a chance to cut the link between Europe and the US, and quietly funded criminal gangs and dissident groups, each with its own agenda. The rifles came with the money.

beats.title: The Home Counties
beats.text: The counties around London were made a protective barrier for the capital, and a Civilian Protection and Continuity Zone for people displaced by forced requisitions, relocations and the fighting.

beats.title: The strikes
beats.text: Then Russian forces captured a key port in Rotterdam and launched ballistic missile strikes on the south of the UK, London included. The Home Counties plan fell apart.

beats.title: Bletchley
beats.text: The government relocated to Bletchley Park, and the streets around it were evacuated: one bag each, and a train to a reception centre. Then the government moved on. Criminals and opportunists moved in.

story.outro: The rest is left lying around the street: leaflets on the doormats, cards in the windows, and the soldiers' logs at the checkpoints.

cta.heading: Early days
cta.text: The Home Counties is in early development, with an early access alpha on the way. New builds, maps and weapons are written up in the dev log as they're added.

features.title: A real place
features.text: The first map, Duncombe Street, is a corner of Bletchley built from real map data: Duncombe Street, Osborne Street, Water Eaton Road, Oliver Road, Clifford Avenue and the old Sainsbury's, beside the West Coast Main Line.

features.title: Loot and extract
features.text: Twelve-minute raids. Search the houses people left in a hurry, the crates and the scavs you drop. Extract before the timer ends, or lose what you were carrying.

features.title: Scavs
features.text: Gang members, chancers and the odd few who never left. They're armed, they take cover, flank in pairs and come to investigate when they hear you.

features.title: Noise
features.text: Sprinting, gunfire and moving through long grass all make noise. Walking, crouching and leaning round corners keep you quieter.

features.title: Gear and weight
features.text: US Army plate carriers next to Russian helmets: NATO kit came through Britain by the shipload, and the gangs brought AKs. Eight gear slots and four pockets, and the more you carry, the slower you move.

features.title: Left behind
features.text: Nobody has cut a hedge since the evacuation. Knee-high grass, wrecked cars, boarded-up houses, and council leaflets still on the doormats.

loop.title: Gear up
loop.text: Choose a loadout. Anything you take in can be lost.

loop.title: Deploy
loop.text: You start at the west or east end of Water Eaton Road, picked at random.

loop.title: Loot
loop.text: Search crates, houses and dead scavs. Keep an eye on your carry weight.

loop.title: Extract
loop.text: The army left its checkpoints when it pulled out. Reach one, find the red smoke and stay in the green zone for ten seconds. If you die, you lose everything you were carrying.
